about.bio: I am an architecture graduate from the Czech Technical University (CTU), holding both Bachelor's and Master's degrees. My background merges architectural design with hands-on, practical experience gained from developer and complex construction projects. I have an excellent command of the BIM-Revit environment, specifically at the detail design stage (DPS) level. Throughout my practice, I have proven my ability to handle independent design work, process complete project documentation, and effectively coordinate different professions.

Junior architect (2024-2025). I collaborated on the design and coordination of large development projects, focusing on layout modifications, common area design, and project documentation. I independently prepared and submitted complete documentation of the actual construction (DSPS). Additionally, I worked closely on preparing documents for authorities, gaining valuable insight into the processes and management of large-scale developments.
Work experience.Metrostav DIZ: Engineer (2022). I participated in the technically and historically demanding reconstruction of the Industrial Palace in Prague. I was responsible for the precise, on-site surveying of existing structures, opening fillings, and atypical wooden and metal elements. I then transformed these field measurements into the detailed drawing documentation required for further implementation phases.
Work experience.Epic Prague: Bartender (2021-present). Working in the extremely dynamic environment of a major Prague club has taught me perfect time management and exceptional stress resistance. I have learned to quickly and effectively resolve crisis situations under pressure while maintaining intensive, daily communication with diverse groups of people.

about.My Path into architecture: My fascination with the built environment began early in childhood. It started playfully—building with Lego and designing virtual spaces in The Sims—but it quickly grew into a genuine passion. I have always had a natural affinity for buildings, constantly observing my surroundings to analyze what makes a space visually compelling and what falls short. This lifelong habit of observing and questioning naturally guided me toward architecture, where I can turn that curiosity into tangible design.
about.My Values: In my architectural practice, I am deeply committed to the principles of sustainability and environmental consciousness. I firmly believe that exceptional design must seamlessly bridge aesthetic appeal with pure, everyday functionality. Visually and conceptually, I am highly inspired by the industrial style—I appreciate its raw honesty, structural clarity, and the way it can be adapted into modern, purposeful spaces.
about.Looking For: I am currently seeking an opportunity where I can fully utilize my skills and find the right professional fit for my continued growth. Specifically, I am looking for a role that allows me to combine my strong architectural background with technical and process precision.

projects.title: Night club DEPOT
projects.description: The diploma project focuses on the design of a nightclub as an architectural insertion into an existing industrial building in Bratislava. The project explores the adaptive reuse of a former technical complex into a contemporary cultural venue, emphasizing the preservation of the original structure, operational flexibility, and the separation of daytime and nighttime activities.

projects.title: Monastery on pilgrimage route
projects.description: In the Baroque farm yard of the Vilémov manor, we propose a monastery, accommodation for pilgrims, and a small brewery. On the site of the original ruined building is the new brewery, which together with the accommodation opposite it forms the western border of the courtyard and forms the entrance from the Via Bohemia pilgrimage route. The monastery extends south of the courtyard and is cut into the sloping ground by its lower storey. It is connected to the chapel, which dominates the courtyard. The functional division of the buildings ensures privacy and silence in the monastery, openness, and transparency in the brewery and accommodation. Connection to and development of the surrounding countryside was important in the design.

projects.title: DPS - Reconstruction of an apartment house
projects.description: The project is dedicated to the complex reconstruction of the original mountain hut in the Jeseníky area, which no longer met the current requirements for recreational housing. The aim was to create quality accommodation with an emphasis on preserving the atmosphere of the place and integration into the natural environment. The architectural design uses a combination of traditional and modern materials - wood, stone and metal - which respond to the local climatic conditions and visually relate to the context of the mountain landscape.

projects.title: Store interior design
projects.description: A tailored interior design for a sports supplements store in Valencia, built around the brand's core philosophy: “Healthy is not a goal, it is a way of living.” The concept merges everyday functionality with a fresh, dynamic aesthetic, utilizing a material palette of light wood, clean white surfaces, and striking blue tile accents. The thoughtfully modified floorplan optimizes customer flow, featuring a custom-made curved reception desk, adaptable modular shelving, and a bold sculptural LED pendant light.

projects.title: Dam Fláje
projects.description: The “Spa upside down“ project is focused on innovative spa concept based on several previous proposals. This work seeks to bring a new perspective to the spa concept, that goes beyond traditional boundaries. In addition to presenting our own proposal, we also choose to present several previous ideas, that have inspired us. The key question at this stage of the project remains, whether the concept of a spa in a dam is really viable and whether it brings measurable benefits for visitors. Is this unconventional idea of a spa centre in such a setting is a really good idea,or just an experiment?
